methodological_rigor.justification: Reanalysis of public TCR sequencing datasets with appropriate bioinformatics tools (ImmunoSEQ, MiTCR). Batch effect correction applied (combat function). However, small heterogeneous sample sizes (9-20 samples across breast/colon cancer, HSCs), no explicit multiplicity correction strategy detailed despite numerous statistical comparisons across diversity indices, CDR3 lengths, V/J genes. Statistical methods include t-tests and ANOVA with Bonferroni mentioned but application scope unclear. Outlier exclusion via Hubert-Vandervieren test appropriate.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 4 (observational bioinformatics analysis of public sequencing data). TCRβ repertoire alterations under RT and immunotherapy documented but no direct clinical outcomes, functional validation, or prognostic utility assessed. No correlation with treatment response or patient survival. Translational path speculative (authors propose TCR diversity as 'predictive biomarker' but no validation provided).

reporting_quality.justification: Bioinformatics methods described in detail (primer design, sequencing platforms, diversity indices). However, multiplicity correction application across analyses unclear. Public datasets cited with DOI and accessible; supplementary figures (S1-S3) referenced but reproducibility limited without explicit code availability statement or deposition of analysis scripts.

novelty_literature.justification: TCRβ repertoire changes under RT and anti-CTLA-4/anti-PD-1 largely known from prior studies (refs 26-27, Rudqvist et al). Present study reanalyzes public data documenting decreased diversity under RT, altered CDR3 length distribution, and V/J gene usage changes—mechanistic confirmation rather than novel discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized methods and results sections with comprehensive figures and statistical comparisons. Discussion extensive with mechanistic hypotheses about thymic damage and immune reconstitution. However, dense statistical presentation and multiple comparisons make interpretation challenging. Some speculative claims about therapeutic optimization unsupported by data.

key_strengths: Multi-dataset bioinformatics analysis with appropriate tools (ImmunoSEQ, MiTCR) and batch effect correction.
Comprehensive evaluation of TCRβ diversity, CDR3 length, V/J gene usage across multiple indices (D50, Gini, Shannon, Simpson).
Systematic analysis of both in-frame (functional) and out-of-frame (pre-selection) repertoires.
Clear documentation of TCRβ alterations associated with RT and immunotherapy.
key_concerns: Multiplicity correction application unclear despite numerous statistical comparisons across conditions and parameters.
Small sample sizes (9-20 per group) across heterogeneous cancer types and HSC conditions; generalizability limited.
No functional validation of predicted TCR diversity-treatment efficacy relationship; findings correlative only.
No clinical endpoints (survival, treatment response, prognostic utility) assessed; translational value unproven.
Code/analysis script availability not explicitly stated; reproducibility limited.
Discussion contains extensive mechanistic speculation (thymic damage, microbiota effects) unsupported by present data.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent bioinformatics reanalysis documenting TCR repertoire alterations under RT and immunotherapy, but methodological concerns (unclear multiplicity correction, small heterogeneous samples) and absence of functional/clinical validation limit contribution. Suitable for tier 4 specialized immunogenomics journals after major revisions clarifying statistical methods.
